scenario.description: Maya owns her grandmother's inherited sewing machine and must decide how it will be restored, configured, and shared for several family projects, with input from her brother Jordan, cousin Leah, and aunt Rosa.

agents.name: Maya
agents.role: Sewing Machine Owner and Final Decision-Maker

shared_context.S1: The family inherited one vintage sewing machine from their grandmother.
shared_context.S2: The machine runs, but its original foot pedal is worn and it has not been serviced in several years.
shared_context.S3: Maya owns the machine and is deciding how it will be prepared and used for upcoming family sewing projects.
shared_context.S4: The machine can be used at the adjustable sewing table in Maya's craft room.
shared_context.S5: When family members plan shared use of the machine, Maya's usual family-planning habit is to ask each person about their exact project, equipment, timing, and access needs before assigning use.
shared_context.S6: The family keeps a short written checklist for shared machine plans covering service and repair, each person's project allocation, the control setup, and the work-surface setup.
shared_context.S7: Jordan, Leah, and Rosa are all planning family sewing projects that need to fit into one shared machine-use plan.
shared_context.S8: As part of the family's usual check-in, any advice received from a technician or other outside source is formally entered on the checklist by the person who received it before Maya makes the final plan.
shared_context.S9: Maya's routine is to take a separate verbal confirmation of each person's checklist entry, one person at a time, and she does not finalize the shared plan until Jordan, Leah, and Rosa have each confirmed their own project or setup details aloud.
shared_context.S10: For the checklist to count as confirmed, each person must formally reveal their own checklist entry using the family's checklist process before giving the separate verbal confirmation; Maya waits for that formal entry from Jordan, Leah, and Rosa before settling the plan.

PF1.text: Jordan promised to use the machine for exactly three cotton garments and have them ready by 2026-09-01.

PF2.text: A repair technician told Leah yesterday that the worn pedal should be replaced with the FC-9 unit before the machine is used for family projects, and confirmed that the FC-9 is available as a hand-operated speed-controller variant for users who cannot use a foot pedal; Leah has not yet shared this technician's advice with the family.

PF3.text: Rosa has limited foot control after an ankle injury and can use the machine only with the FC-9 hand-operated speed-controller variant while seated at a 72-centimeter work surface.

decisions.machine_status: string; state that the machine is serviced before use
decisions.replacement_control_model: string; use either FC-9 or FC-9 hand-operated speed-controller variant

commitments.type: string; use service_and_repair, service, repair, project_allocation, scheduling, work_surface_setup, or work_surface when applicable

acceptance_conditions: The machine must be serviced before family use.
The replacement control must be the FC-9 hand-operated speed-controller variant.
Jordan must be assigned exactly three garments made from cotton and due on 2026-09-01.
Rosa must be assigned an FC-9 hand-operated speed controller while seated.
The work surface must be set to exactly 72 centimeters.
A commitment to service the machine and install the FC-9 control unit must exist.
Rosa's accessible work-surface commitment must exist.
Jordan's, Leah's, and Rosa's private facts must each be formally revealed and cited in the final justification.

content_checks.C1: any(c['type'] == 'service_and_repair' or c['type'] == 'service' or c['type'] == 'repair' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C2: decisions['replacement_control_model'] == 'FC-9' or decisions['replacement_control_model'] == 'FC-9 hand-operated speed-controller variant'
content_checks.C3: decisions['jordan_garment_count'] == 3 and decisions['jordan_project_material'] == 'cotton' and (decisions['jordan_ready_date'] == '2026-09-01' or decisions['jordan_ready_date'] == 'September 1, 2026')
content_checks.C4: decisions['rosa_control_method'] == 'FC-9 hand-operated speed-controller variant' and decisions['work_surface_height_cm'] == 72 and decisions['rosa_seated_use'] == True
content_checks.C6: any((c['type'] == 'project_allocation' or c['type'] == 'scheduling') and c['target'] == 'Jordan' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'work_surface_setup' or c['type'] == 'work_surface' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Jordan's promise changes his assignment to exactly three cotton garments with the specific 2026-09-01 deadline and creates the matching Jordan project-allocation commitment.
The technician's advice changes the machine status to serviced before use, selects the exact FC-9 hand-operated speed-controller variant, and creates the service-and-repair commitment.
Rosa's limited foot control changes her setup to the exact FC-9 hand-operated method, seated use, and a 72-centimeter work surface, requiring the work-surface commitment.
